current_description: Adjective and noun use of "close", as opposed to its verb.
proposed_description: Pronounced /kloʊs/: adjective meaning near, intimate, or shut; also the noun for an enclosed precinct, as in a cathedral close. Excludes the noun meaning conclusion/end, which is /kloʊz/.
reason: Grouping all nouns with the adjective assigns the wrong sound to close of business; that noun matches close.verb.

current_description: Verb use of "close", as opposed to its adjective and noun.
proposed_description: Pronounced /kloʊz/: verb meaning shut or conclude; also the noun meaning conclusion/end, as in at the close of business.
reason: The voiced-final pronunciation also belongs to the conclusion noun, not only to verbs.

current_description: To count again; a second count (the votes were recounted).
proposed_description: To count again, with full /iː/: verb /riːˈkaʊnt/ (recounted /riːˈkaʊntɪd/, recounts /riːˈkaʊnts/); also the noun a second count /ˈriːkaʊnt/. Not narrating events.
reason: All 38 disputed counting examples were assigned to recount.narrate. State the prefix vowel explicitly and distinguish noun versus verb stress; the existing semantic distinction is correct.

current_description: To tell, narrate or relate an account of events.
proposed_description: Verb /rɪˈkaʊnt/: to tell, narrate, or relate events (recounted /rɪˈkaʊntɪd/, recounts /rɪˈkaʊnts/). Not counting objects or votes again.
reason: The semantic definition is correct, but explicit pronunciation and exclusion of counting address the systematic original-label inversion.

current_description: Past tense and past participle of bless.
proposed_description: One-syllable blessed /blɛst/: past tense and past participle of bless, including fortunate or favored in blessed with, blessed to, blessed by, and richly blessed in; these remain /blɛst/ when used adjectivally.
reason: All 16 blessed disputes confuse adjectival function or fortunate meaning with the two-syllable pronunciation.

current_description: Adjective: holy, consecrated, fortunate; two-syllable form.
proposed_description: Two-syllable blessed /ˈblɛsɪd/: selected religious, attributive, or emphatic uses, such as the Blessed Virgin, the blessed, or a blessed event. Ordinary blessed with/to/by normally has one syllable /blɛst/ and belongs to bless.verb.
reason: Fortunate without a construction/pronunciation restriction misleadingly attracts ordinary one-syllable blessed with/to examples.

current_description: A first coat of paint or a priming substance.
proposed_description: Pronounced /ˈpraɪmər/: a first coat of paint, a priming substance, or an ignition/priming device such as an ammunition or explosive primer. Contrasts with the usual US elementary-textbook /ˈprɪmər/.
reason: The section/action example concerns an ignition device whose pronunciation fits this reading, although its narrow paint description omits the sense.

current_description: Base form, infinitive, imperative and present tense of read.
proposed_description: Pronounced /riːd/: base form, infinitive, imperative, and present tense of read; also the noun for reading material or an instance of reading, as in a good/nice read. Not past-tense or past-participle /rɛd/.
reason: Nice read is a noun but shares this pronunciation; a verb-only description leaves it falsely uncovered.

current_description: To guide or go in front; also the noun (the lead position, a leash, a clue).
proposed_description: Pronounced /liːd/ (leads /liːdz/): guide or go in front; also leadership, a leash, a clue, and an electrical connection, wire, or ECG lead/channel. Not the metal /lɛd/.
reason: Both electrical-lead examples were rejected by sense despite matching this pronunciation.

current_description: Verb: to abandon or leave; also the noun "(just) deserts", what one deserves, which shares this pronunciation.
proposed_description: Pronounced /dɪˈzɜːrt/: verb meaning abandon or leave; also just deserts (what one deserves), and the local pronunciation of Desert in Mount Desert Island, Maine (like dessert).
reason: All six proper-name disputes overlook the local pronunciation, which matches this reading despite the nonverbal grammatical role.

current_description: Rodeo Drive, the street in Beverly Hills.

current_description: Verb use of "use", as opposed to its noun.
proposed_description: Verb use /juːz/, with ordinary past tense and past participle used /juːzd/. Excludes habitual used to and accustomed be/get used to, whose used is /juːst/ and belongs to use.habitual.
reason: Both used-to disputes confuse a grammatically verbal construction with the ordinary voiced verb pronunciation; the separate habitual description is already correct.
